name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with system preference as the default dark mode, but add a persistent toggle in settings. This matches the dark themes of Manus and Graphify, ensuring consistency with user expectations and reducing visual fatigue during long sessions. The trade-off is a slight increase in initial setup complexity, but the benefit of immediate familiarity outweighs it.

name: Pane
text: The real risk is locking users into a choice they may regret—once they toggle dark mode, they’re stuck with it unless they dig into settings. Instead, ship a one-time selector that remembers their preference but lets them change it anytime without friction. Settle it by testing both: measure how often users switch modes and whether they abandon the tool after toggling.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with a one-time dark/light mode selector at first launch, defaulting to system preference. This forces users to make a deliberate choice upfront, avoiding the "stuck" feeling of a persistent toggle while still respecting their system’s default. The trade-off is a minor initial friction—users must decide immediately—but it prevents later regret and keeps the interface clean. Consistency with Manus and Graphify’s dark themes is maintained without locking anyone into a bad default.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A one-time selector still locks users into a choice they may regret—what if they toggle once, then later realize it clashes with their workflow? The better alternative is a persistent, easily accessible toggle in the top bar, not buried in settings. Settle it by measuring how often users change their preference after the first week—if it’s rare, the one-time approach wins; if frequent, the toggle does.
